name: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12
lead: Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12, sold as Biopeptide EL, is a synthetic fatty-acid-linked peptide derived from a repeating elastin sequence and used in anti-ageing creams. It is marketed as supporting skin elasticity.

A 2025 laboratory study using label-free imaging techniques examined its short-term effects on human skin composition and mechanics, describing it as a self-assembling peptide with potential skincare benefits [1]. No clinical trial results were found.

paras: The peptide is promoted in anti-ageing products for firmness and elasticity. Researchers describe cosmetic self-assembling peptides of this kind as interacting with skin structures, though the short-term impact on composition and mechanics had been unclear before the 2025 study [1].
No studies found. A 2025 ex vivo/experimental study monitored the peptide in human skin layers with non-invasive techniques and assessed its mechanical interaction with skin components [1].
A 2026 paper proposes a framework for safety evaluation of cosmetic peptides generally, as the industry shifts away from animal testing [2]. No ingredient-specific adverse-effect data were found.

card.summary: An elastin-fragment cosmetic peptide (Biopeptide EL) with lab-level evidence and no clinical trials found.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl hexapeptide-12 is a lab-made peptide based on an elastin sequence, added to anti-ageing creams for elasticity.

Only early laboratory research exists; no clinical trial was found.
quick.mechanism: It is described as a self-assembling peptide that interacts with skin components and may alter skin mechanics, based on a 2025 imaging study.
quick.risks: No ingredient-specific harms were found; safety frameworks for cosmetic peptides are still evolving.
